status: Accepted as a fixed-parameter latent-population identification lemma; no observed-response identification claim

source_review.finding: Read actual local source hierarchy. Source common effect has mean mu; centering it and subtracting it from familial effects yields independent Gaussian genetic innovations. The DZ two-stage variance halves give genetic variance va and cross covariance va/2; MZ shares a single genetic effect. Residual variance depends on genetic A, not on total familial F or centered C. Conditional residual independence is the model assumption required throughout.

independent_step_checks.finding: C=C_source-mu is centered and independent of genetic innovations. Theta=mu+A+C+sqrt(ve*exp(beta*A))*Z therefore includes mu exactly once. ETheta=mu because E[Z|A,C]=0.

At fixed finite va,vc,ve,beta, every positive-integer absolute residual moment factors into ve^(k/2)*E exp(k*beta*A/2)*E|Z|^k, finite by the Gaussian exponential moment. Gaussian A+C also has finite absolute moments. The stated sum inequality establishes finite absolute central moments. Products needed for covariance and cubic expansion are integrable. This uses neither a marginal-trait moment-generating function nor any prior averaging.

Conditional residual cross product is H1*H2*E[Z1*Z2]=0; a shared random variance scale in MZ does not imply shared residual innovations. All residual versus genetic/common cross terms vanish by conditional centering. Thus K_MZ=va+vc and K_DZ=va/2+vc, including nonzero beta.

Total variance yields T=va+vc+R with R=ve*exp(beta^2*va/2)>0. ve is the conditional variance at genetic A0; it is not the marginal residual variance R unless beta=0. In particular the beta0 notation denotes log baseline environmental variance, distinct from the interaction coefficient beta.

Independently expanding conditional on A,C leaves (A+C)^3+3*(A+C)*ve*exp(beta*A). The first expectation is0 and the C term is0 by independence/centering. Completing the square gives exp(beta*a)*phi_va(a)=exp(beta^2*va/2)*phi_va(a-va*beta), hence E[A exp(beta*A)]=va*beta*exp(beta^2*va/2). Therefore m3=3*va*beta*R, with correct factor3 and sign.

Two zygosity covariances identify va=2*(K_MZ-K_DZ) and vc=2*K_DZ-K_MZ. T then identifies R. Since va,R>0, beta=m3/(3*va*R) is unique; beta0=log(R)-beta^2*va/2 and mu=mean are unique. This is an explicit global inverse on moments arising from the stated domain, not parameter counting or a claim that arbitrary moment vectors are admissible.

At va0 the interaction vanishes for all beta and identification fails; excluded correctly. At vc0 the fixed-parameter calculations remain valid with degenerate centered C, although the source prior is interior. ve0 is outside finite beta0 and would also erase interaction. For beta=0 the trait pair is Gaussian; for beta nonzero, va,R>0 force nonzero finite m3 and hence a non-Gaussian marginal.

exact_checks.method: Re-executed submitted exact SymPy assertions with output write suppressed. All dependency hashes match. Independently reviewed the probability and exponential-tilting derivations; symbolic fixtures do not replace independence/integrability arguments.

limits: The inverse is for the latent trait coordinate. No new proof makes the finitely many calibrated Rasch response-pattern probabilities identify these latent moments. The known-Gaussian item lemma cannot be applied for nonzero beta.

Known genetic correlations, same components across both zygosity populations, both population laws and the stated independent innovations are substantive conditions. The theorem does not transfer to one-zygosity or different-component designs.
Fixed-parameter moment existence does not imply prior-predictive finite moments: the source InvGamma(1,1) variances have infinite mean. No prior averaging or posterior-moment theorem is used.
Latent moment identification does not imply good conditioning, finite-MLE uniqueness/existence, unbiased recovery, significance/power or sampler convergence.
No formal proof-assistant certification supplied. Ordinary analytical acceptance leaves all broad scientific statuses and missing observed-response bridge unchanged.
operations: Only this independent review record created; author scripts/outputs and running model files unchanged; no sampling, integration or Monte Carlo.
